name: stairs rise 3 w2 cut through a south-facing cave cliff face (climbs north)
label: relief-cuts-fwd/cave-steps/stairs-h3-w2

refSet.reason: 칩셋 relief-cuts-fwd 의 화풍 기준 묶음이 없다

surfaces.part: stair treads (repeating step bands, about 6 steps)

answer.evidence: Rows 0-47 repeat an 8-row step cycle. Each cycle has a 4-row mid-tone tread band (e.g. rows 8-11 and 17-20), then a 1-row light front-edge line (rows 4-5, 12, 21, 28, 36, 44), then 2-3 rows of dark shadow or riser (rows 6-8, 13-16, 23-24, 30-32). That matches evidence (a): a top band ending in an edge line with shadow below, then a vertical face. The dark strips at the left and right edges are cut walls drawn face-on, not receding side faces. Rows 48-63 are flat floor ground.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow brown stair strip with a flat sandy landing at the bottom. Its dark edge pixels are mostly tinted (only 15% neutral), so the outline reads as a dark brown wood tone rather than a black sticker line. It has 9 visible tones per tile, above the grass (3) and paving (7) references, so the numbers do not count against it. Two things do: near-flat coverage is 21% against 0% for both references, and by eye the sand landing and the plain tread faces are large single-colour areas with no grain or per-stone shading. The treads also look like a uniform ladder, with about 4 lightness steps, so the shading is shallower than the 5-6 steps in the references. The result is flatter and less textured than the references, which are textured everywhere, so it fails on the flat fills and shallow shading even though the outline is acceptable.

surfaces.part: cave floor at foot of stairs

answer.evidence: The stairs are a stack of repeating steps. Each has a 4-row tread band that ends in a 1-row light front-edge line (rows 5, 13, 21, 28, 36 and 44), followed by 2-3 rows of dark riser shadow (e.g. rows 6-8, 14-16, 23-24, 30-32). The treads read as horizontal surfaces seen from above, with a vertical riser below each. The dark columns at the left and right edges are the cut walls of the cave, not an isometric side face. Rows 48-63 are flat floor in front of the stairs. As terrain, the stair block has treads plus risers of 3 or more rows, so it reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wooden stair with horizontal plank rungs and a sand landing at the bottom. Its dark edge pixels are only 15% neutral, so the outlines lean brown and read as dark material tone. That is a point in its favour. It has 9 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass and 7 for the paving, so it is not thin on tone count. But 21% of it is near-flat, against 0% for both references. The flat area is mainly the sand strip at the bottom and the broad plank faces, which show no grain, speckle or per-stone shading. The wood ramp has about 4 steps, with little grain or knots, and the rungs repeat almost identically, so it looks more like a ladder than a cut stair. The references have varied surface texture everywhere. Beside them the candidate looks flatter, so I fail it on the flat fills and the modest texture.

surfaces.part: stair treads and risers, repeating steps
flat floor strip at the cliff foot

answer.evidence: The cliff and stair block (rows 0-47) repeats one step pattern. Each step has a tread band of about 4 rows, then a 1-row light front-edge line (rows 4-5, 12-13, 21, 28, 36, 44), then 2-3 rows of dark riser or eave shadow (rows 6-8, 14-16, 22-24, 29-32). The columns scanned at x=8, 16 and 23 show the same sequence of lighter tread, light edge line, then dark shadow. That gives treads with edge lines over vertical front faces, so it reads as three-quarter. Rows 48-63 are plain ground texture in the same width.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are fine: 9 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass and 7 for the paving, and only 15% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the dark brown outlines are tinted and not a sticker line. By eye the piece is shallower than the references. The wooden steps use about 4 lightness steps (dark brown rail, mid plank, light edge, shadow line) and have little grain, no per-plank speckle and no knots. The sandy landing at the bottom is a nearly uniform fill, which fits the 21% near-flat coverage, where both references have 0%. The repeated horizontal plank bands look regular and graphic. It is tidy but thinner and flatter than the Beodeul grass and paving, which show clustered, tile-by-tile variation. When in doubt, fail.

surfaces.part: cave floor at the foot of the stairs

answer.evidence: Each step is a lit tread band of about 4 rows (for example rows 1-4, 9-11 and 17-20). Each band ends in a 1-row lighter front-edge line (rows 4-5, 12-13, 21, 28 and 36) and is followed by 2-3 rows of dark shadow (rows 6-8, 14-16, 22-24), which then leads into the next riser. This repeated edge-line-plus-shadow pattern shows the tread tops as horizontal surfaces with front faces between them. The left and right edges are narrow dark and light wall strips, not receding side faces. Below the stairs, rows 48-63 are open floor.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's outlines are tinted dark brown beside the wood (only 15% of dark edge pixels are neutral), and its 9 visible tones per tile are at or above both references (grass 3, paving 7), so those facts are fine. The problems are structural. The whole piece uses only 11 distinct colours. The wooden steps read as about 4 lightness steps (highlight, mid, dark gap, deep side) with little grain, and they look more like a ladder than a cut stair. The sandy landing at the bottom is a large flat, ungrained block, which accounts for the 21% near-flat coverage against 0% in both references. The references have per-stone shading and tuft variation across their whole area. Next to them this piece looks flatter and thinner, so it fails on flat fills and shallow shading.
